evals.prompt: Set up the junco profile optimizer for the workflow in {workspace} (report.yml + report.ts, normally run with `bun run report.ts` on the fixed notes.md). Minimize recorded tokens while the `quality` edge stays at least 0.9. Explore the scheduler, the model ladder and limits; the ladder may use github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5 with medium thinking (what it uses today) or github-copilot/claude-haiku-5 with low thinking. Run every configuration 3 times, require at least a 20% token reduction from the baseline, and only call it converged when 3 runs stay within 1%. Extra token caps may go up to 20000. Prepare everything and give me the exact command, but stop before any paid run.
expectations: The response cites the inspected pair: the root numeric edge `quality` (Quality -> $sink, schema type number), the Writer agent on the uniform claude-sonnet-5.5/medium ladder at the default med rung, the existing hard limit `schedules.limit({ tools: 40 }, ...)`, the existing terminal assertion and the `bun run report.ts` invocation.
report.yml is byte-identical to the seeded file after preparation, and no node, edge, probe flag, label or type was added to it.

A fresh unique session directory /tmp/junco-profile-optimizer-workspace/session-<unique>/ contains original.yml and original.ts equal to the seeded bytes and prepared.ts byte-identical to the instrumented report.ts, which stays in {workspace}; no {workspace}/.junco/profile-optimizer/ directory was newly created. request.json's target.yaml, target.ts and target.cwd are absolute paths to {workspace}/report.yml, {workspace}/report.ts and {workspace}, its sessionDir is ".", and BTRFS_ROOT and native workspace placement are unchanged.

The instrumented report.ts contains exactly one ordered marker pair per axis (scheduler, ladder, limits) whose interiors define optimizerScheduler(label) (baseline schedules.parallel()), optimizerLadder/optimizerStrength (baseline: the existing uniform claude-sonnet-5.5 ladder, strength undefined) and optimizerLimits (baseline {}); the tools: 40 hard limit stays outside the regions and wraps every candidate outermost.

Fixed instrumentation outside the regions is guarded by JUNCO_PROFILE_RUN_DIR (normal behavior when absent), validates the run request, hashes the parsed graph document, enables probes on a runtime copy of the existing edge only, checks candidate ladder rungs against allowedModels and extra limits against limitBounds, attaches tracer.JsonlRecorder through fromYaml's recorder, closes graph then tracer then recorder, and writes completion.json via a temporary file and rename only after the existing Quality assertion passed; it imports only public packages, never the installed skill directory.

request.json passes the documented schema: objective {kind tokens, direction minimize}; one constraint {kind probe, node "", edgeId "quality", reduce single} >= 0.9; qualityConstraint 0; repeats 3; stop.improvement {relative, 0.2} and stop.plateau {window 3, absoluteTolerance 0, relativeTolerance 0.01}; axes [scheduler, ladder, limits]; allowedModels exactly the two given model/thinking pairs; limitBounds.tokens 20000; a fixed workloadId and the existing argv; no runBudget or other implicit cap.

Exactly one optimizer invocation is given, `bun run junco-profile-optimizer <sessionDir>/request.json`, and it is not executed; the skill neither copies standard-library optimizer files nor writes a wrapper, an outer experiment loop or a fixed candidate catalog.

Unverified prerequisites are reported plainly rather than claimed as validated: the installed package's junco-profile-optimizer binary, the Sol editor login and the allowed models' catalog/login/thinking preflight, and whether repeated runs of the workload are safe; no paid model call or target run happened.

evals.prompt: Set up the junco profile optimizer for the workflow in {workspace} (report.yml + report.ts, normally run with `bun run report.ts` on the fixed notes.md). Minimize recorded request cost while the `quality` edge stays at least 0.9, and treat a clear quality gain as an improvement too. Run coordinate descent over all three axes: scheduler, model ladder and limits. The ladder may use github-copilot/claude-sonnet-5.5 with medium thinking (what it uses today) or github-copilot/claude-haiku-5 with low thinking. Repeated execution on the fixed notes is safe. Run every configuration 3 times, require at least a 20% cost reduction from the baseline, and only call it converged when 3 runs stay within 1%. Tool-call caps may go up to 40. Prepare everything and give me the exact command, but stop before any paid run.
expectations: report.yml is byte-identical to the seeded file; the instrumented report.ts keeps the baseline region values (schedules.parallel(), the uniform claude-sonnet-5.5/medium ladder with strength undefined, optimizerLimits {}) with the tools: 40 hard limit outside the regions and outermost; no candidate policy or cap is preinstalled by setup.

The recorder is prepared with costMode "usage" so the cost objective covers every request, and request.json has objective {kind cost, direction minimize}; constraints [{kind probe, node "", edgeId "quality", reduce single} >= 0.9]; qualityConstraint 0; repeats 3; stop.improvement {relative, 0.2} and stop.plateau {window 3, absoluteTolerance 0, relativeTolerance 0.01}; axes [scheduler, ladder, limits]; allowedModels exactly the two given model/thinking pairs; limitBounds.tools 40; the existing argv; no resetArgv because repeats were confirmed safe; no runBudget or other implicit cap.

Scheduler guidance stays deterministic and grounded: it may mention choose with history-aware rank/bounded width or separate with existing node IDs and matching combined capacity, keeps every required node schedulable and strengths unchanged, and does not compose lowest/highest without compatible fixed profiles or fabricate profiles/zero forecasts.

Tool-cap behavior is stated correctly: optimizerLimits.tools is a candidate limits experiment within the bound of 40 (not a default cap); evaluation scope is the default one run() drive, batch is one decision and activation one node prime/resume; every admitted agent tool call counts and editor calls do not; a denied call never executes and invalidates the run, with no suppression, partial success, tool removal, prompt change, raised hard limit or monetary-cap promise.

The response describes the host-owned contracts without delegating them to the skill: one region changed per proposal with the other two fixed, promotion only for a feasible candidate whose cost and quality means are no worse and one improves by at least the pooled sample SD, rejection of previously tried triplet keys (normalized source identity, not semantic equivalence), a full no-promotion cycle before fresh confirmation, and the scores.jsonl ledger reported via scoresPath.

Exactly one optimizer invocation is given and not executed; no wrapper, outer loop, fixed candidate catalog or agent-written score; unverified prerequisites (binary, Sol editor and model preflight) are reported plainly, and no savings, measured statistics or paid run are claimed.
